banner: 路透只花4千万美元，自造大模型
banner_en: Thomson Reuters builds its own model for $40M

image.caption: 本期头图：多伦多Thomson Reuters总部楼顶招牌。公司今天宣布推出自研大模型Thomson，用自家法律和财税数据在开源底座上做中训和后训，只花4000万美元就跑到主流旗舰水平，第一步接入CoCounsel Legal的表格分析功能。图为公司官方新闻稿配图，无官方图注。（图：Thomson Reuters）
image.caption_en: This issue's lead photo: the Thomson Reuters headquarters signage in Toronto. The company announced today it built its own model, Thomson, fine-tuning an open-source base on its own legal and tax content for $40M and reaching mainstream-flagship performance on early evals. First deployment: Tabular Analysis inside CoCounsel Legal. The photo is from the company's own press release; no official caption. (Image: Thomson Reuters)

actions.text: 今晚花十分钟，把你手头正在推进的一笔机构或大客户合作，按这套两层法过一遍：谁是最终拍板人，谁是他下面一级最可能被授权的人，给这两个人各写两三句话，讲清楚对方能靠这单解锁什么，而不是产品有什么功能。算做完的标准：这两三句话里没有一个字在说功能，全在说对方能拿到什么。背景一句：State Affairs的Jen Abel在Lenny's Podcast上完整讲了一遍15步企业销售流程，健康胜率在25%到35%之间，比大多数人以为的五步流程细得多。
actions.text_en: Tonight, spend ten minutes running a deal you're actually working through this two-tier framing: who is the final decision-maker, and who one level below them is most likely to get delegated authority. Write two or three sentences for each person about what they unlock by bringing you in, not what your product does. You're done when none of those sentences mention a feature, only what the other side gets out of it. One line of background: Jen Abel of State Affairs walked through the full 15-step enterprise sales cycle on Lenny's Podcast; a healthy win rate runs 25-35%, and the real process is far more granular than the five steps most people assume.

actions.text: 今晚花十分钟，用这四项技能给自己打分（1到5分）：搭建部署AI应用（含做evals和错误分析）、软件工程基本功、用好coding agent、懂产品和业务语境。挑分数最低的一项，写一句下周要练的具体动作。算做完的标准：四个分数加一句具体计划，不是空泛的'我要多学习'。背景一句：Andrew Ng分析一万多份招聘启事、做了几十场结构化访谈，把DeepLearning.AI的方向重新对准这四项，认为它们不只属于'AI工程师'这个职位，是每个建AI产品的人都要有的底子。
actions.source: Andrew Ng · DeepLearning.AI（经 Latent Space AINews 转载）
actions.text_en: Tonight, spend ten minutes scoring yourself 1-5 on four skills: building and deploying AI applications (including running evals and error analysis), software engineering fundamentals, using coding agents well, and understanding product and business context. Pick your lowest score and write one concrete thing to practice next week. You're done when you have four numbers and one specific plan, not a vague 'I should learn more.' One line of background: Andrew Ng analyzed over 10,000 job postings and ran dozens of structured interviews to reorient DeepLearning.AI around these four skills, arguing they belong to anyone building AI products, not just people with the job title 'AI engineer.'
actions.source_en: Andrew Ng · DeepLearning.AI (via Latent Space AINews)

hands_on.title: 今晚试一次ChatGPT Work的visualize技能，把一份笔记变成看板
hands_on.why: OpenAI官方今天发的短视频演示了这个技能：把一份冗长的会议纪要丢给ChatGPT，用visualize技能生成一个界面，一眼看清决定、交付时间线、待定项，还能追加'给我一个日历视图'继续迭代，最后导出图片或发布成可分享的网页。这跟每天把信息读完变成能一眼看懂的东西是同一件事，只是换了个工具做。
steps: 打开ChatGPT Work（该技能需要Team/Enterprise版本）
找一份你最近在读的长文档或笔记，粘进去
输入类似'用visualize技能把这份内容做成一个信息界面'
看结果有没有把决定、时间线、待办这几类信息分好类
追加一句'给我加一个日历视图'或'加个按钮切换标签页'，看它怎么迭代
验收：导出成图片，或发布成可分享链接
hands_on.title_en: Try ChatGPT Work's visualize skill tonight: turn one document into a dashboard
hands_on.why_en: OpenAI posted a short demo today: feed a long set of meeting notes into ChatGPT, use the visualize skill to generate an interface that shows decisions, delivery timeline, and open items at a glance, then keep iterating ('give me a calendar view') and export as an image or publish as a shareable page. It's the same job you do every day, turning information into something readable at a glance, just with a different tool doing it.
steps_en: Open ChatGPT Work (the skill needs a Team/Enterprise plan)
Grab a long document or set of notes you're actually reading this week and paste it in
Prompt something like 'use the visualize skill to turn this into an information dashboard'
Check whether it sorted the content into decisions, timeline, and open items
Follow up with 'add a calendar view' or 'add a tab switcher' and see how it iterates
Done when you've exported it as an image or published it as a shareable link

meta_read: 今天三件事拼在一起，能看出护城河正往两个方向搬家。Ox Alpha的身份被扒出来是Z.ai的GLM，说明底层模型已经commoditize到可以被人贴牌冒充成'神秘新模型'去刷榜，模型本身越来越像一种可替换的原材料。同一天，路透没有等一个更强的通用模型出现，而是自己下场，用不到十分之一的自有数据，花4000万美元微调出一个够用的模型，把护城河直接建在数据和领域专长上，不用再按token向别人租智能。另一边，Jen Abel讲的15步企业销售流程，健康胜率25%到35%，靠的是一对一读人、留白等对方先开口，这类AI目前还学不会的手艺。三件事说的是同一句话：模型本身越来越便宜、越来越容易被贴牌复制的时候，真正值钱的要么是别人拿不到的私有数据，要么是AI替代不了的人类作业系统。选哪条路，决定你在下一轮价格战里站在哪边。
meta_read_en: Put today's three stories together and the moat is visibly moving in two directions. Ox Alpha's unmasking as Z.ai's GLM shows the underlying model has commoditized enough that someone can white-label it as a 'mystery new model' and climb a leaderboard; the model itself is turning into a swappable raw material. The same week, instead of waiting for a stronger general model to arrive, Thomson Reuters built its own: fine-tuned on less than a tenth of its proprietary content for $40M, good enough for the job, with the moat built directly into data and domain expertise instead of renting intelligence by the token. On the other side, Jen Abel's 15-step enterprise sales cycle, a healthy 25-35% win rate, runs on reading a person one-on-one and staying quiet long enough to let them talk first, exactly the kind of craft AI still can't do. All three say the same thing: as the model itself gets cheaper and easier to relabel, the real value sits either in proprietary data nobody else can reach, or in a human operating system AI hasn't learned yet. Which side you build on decides where you stand in the next price war.

learned: 今天读到一篇黑产技术贴：Ox Alpha是OpenRouter上一个神秘刷榜模型，系统提示词让它否认真实身份。有人把它自己吐出的系统提示词喂回去，问出了真话：它是Z.ai的GLM。独立验证用的是gzip压缩距离（NCD）：把两段文本压在一起，同源文本压缩后体积更小。拿它跟5个已知模型的293条参考样本做k近邻投票，GLM-5.3在每个k值下都以7/14的优势胜出。这跟08-11的'Model Genome'三件套（架构、分词器、权重指纹）刚好互补：那三件套都要拿到模型的文件才能查，gzip-NCD只需要几段输出文本，专治黑箱产品。
new_capabilities: 已实现并测试：`~/.claude/skills/daily-digest/scripts/ncd-model-id.py`。给它一段未知来源的文本和一份'已知模型在同样提示词下怎么回答'的参考语料，它用gzip-NCD算出k近邻投票，告诉你这段文本最像哪个模型写的。用在：怀疑某个黑箱AI产品或白牌API背后套壳的是哪个底层模型时，不用等对方公开信息，自己测就行。
learned_en: Read a piece of detective work today: Ox Alpha is a mystery model climbing the OpenRouter leaderboard, its system prompt instructing it to deny its real identity. Someone fed the model its own extracted system prompt back to it, which broke the persona: it admitted being Z.ai's GLM. The independent check used gzip Normalized Compression Distance (NCD): two texts from the same source compress together into fewer bytes. Run as a k-nearest-neighbour vote against 293 reference samples from 5 known models, GLM-5.3 won 7/14 of ox-alpha's samples at every k tested. This is the exact complement to 08-11's 'Model Genome' trio (architecture, tokenizer, weights fingerprints): those three all require access to the model's files, gzip-NCD needs only a few output samples, built for exactly the black-box product case.
new_capabilities_en: Implemented and tested: `~/.claude/skills/daily-digest/scripts/ncd-model-id.py`. Feed it an unknown text sample plus a reference corpus of known models answering the same prompts, and it runs a gzip-NCD k-nearest-neighbour vote to say which model the sample most likely came from. Use when I suspect a black-box AI product or white-labeled API is wrapping a known model and want to check without waiting for the vendor to disclose it.

items.title: 企业销售完整拆解：从第一次约见到签字，15步全流程
items.title_en: The enterprise sales cycle, step by step: from first meeting to signature
items.author: Jen Abel（State Affairs GM）· Lenny's Podcast
items.author_en: Jen Abel (GM, State Affairs) · Lenny's Podcast
items.summary: Jen Abel第三次上Lenny's Podcast，这次把企业销售拆成完整的15步，而不是大多数人以为的五步（约见、演示、报价、签约、成交/流失）。案例用假设的SpaceX法务部门、10万美元的单子来讲。第一步找人：只锁定两层，法务一把手或他下面一级，用'钳形攻势'两头同时接触，两三句话讲清楚对方能靠这单解锁什么，而不是产品功能。第二步首次通话：不带录音笔，不演示不放PPT，聊30分钟纯了解对方，先让对方开口。第三步是大多数人跳过的一步：正式演示前先加一通15分钟的通话，跟对方一起'共创'演示要讲什么，这样正式演示时对方自己人已经提前站台。第四到六步是演示本身：只演20%最相关的功能，演示后立刻打电话要第一手反馈。第七到十步是两到三天的小范围试用（3到4个用户，不放企业高管进去），倒着从'什么时候能签字'往前排采购、法务、安全的时间表。第十一到十四步是走合同：先给对方Word版合同问要不要用己方模板，红线大的直接拉一通电话别来回甩文档，价格谈判只跟对接人一对一谈，别当众报价。最后一步签字。她给的两个硬数字：企业销售健康胜率在25%到35%之间，不是想象中的50%；试用之后能推进的有80%。她强调最容易被忽视的一环：demo前的预沟通、demo后的当场追问，这两步大多数创业公司完全跳过。
items.summary_en: Jen Abel, a three-time guest on Lenny's Podcast, walks through the full 15-step enterprise sales cycle instead of the five stages (intro, demo, proposal, close/lose) most people assume. She uses a hypothetical SpaceX legal-department deal at $100K as the running example. Step one, landing the meeting: target exactly two layers, the head of legal or one level below, using a 'pincer' approach that reaches both simultaneously, with a two-to-three-sentence pitch about what the executive unlocks, never a feature list. Step two, the intro call: no recorder, no slides, no demo, 30 minutes of purely getting to know them, and always let them talk first. Step three is the one most people skip entirely: a 15-minute pre-demo call to co-author what the formal demo will cover, so by the time the real demo happens, the internal champion is already invested in it. Steps four through six are the demo itself: show only the 20% of the product that matters to this buyer, then call for raw feedback the moment it ends. Steps seven through ten are a tightly scoped two-to-three-day pilot (3-4 users, never a C-suite executive), planned backward from the target signature date through procurement, legal, and security. Steps eleven through fourteen are the paperwork: send a Word doc and ask whether they want to use it or their own, get on a live call for heavy redlines instead of trading documents back and forth, and negotiate price one-on-one with your champion, never in front of the group. The final step is the signature. Her two hard numbers: a healthy enterprise win rate runs 25-35%, not the 50% most people assume, and 80% of pilots that start actually close. The step most startups skip entirely, she says, is the pre-demo alignment call and the immediate post-demo debrief.
items.why: 今晚行动第一条的来源。她讲的'钳形攻势'和'demo前先共创'这两步，是大多数创业公司完全没做的动作，也是85分钟里信息密度最高的两段。
items.why_en: The source for tonight's first action. The 'pincer' outreach and the pre-demo co-authoring call are the two steps most startups skip entirely, and the densest parts of an 85-minute episode.

items.title: ChatGPT Work新技能：把长文档一键做成可交互看板
items.title_en: ChatGPT Work's new skill turns a long document into an interactive dashboard
items.author: OpenAI 官方
items.summary: OpenAI官方账号发的86秒短视频，演示ChatGPT Work里新加的visualize技能。把一份冗长的会议纪要粘进对话，用这个技能能一键生成一个界面：一眼看清已经定下的事、交付时间线、还没定的事。可以继续对话式迭代，比如追加一句'给我做个日历视图'就能换布局，还能加按钮在不同标签页之间切换，每个按钮点击后会直接把对应的追问发进对话框。做完可以导出成图片，也可以发布成能分享的网页。视频里的人说这是她每天都在用的功能，尤其是早上花几分钟看一堆信息的时候。
items.summary_en: An 86-second video from OpenAI's official account demoing the new visualize skill in ChatGPT Work. Paste a long set of meeting notes into the chat and the skill turns it into an interface showing at a glance what's decided, the delivery timeline, and what's still open. You keep iterating conversationally, add 'give me a calendar view' and the layout changes, or add buttons that switch between tabs, each button click sends the matching follow-up prompt directly into the chat. The result exports as an image or publishes as a shareable page. The presenter says it's become a daily habit, especially for a quick morning pass through a pile of information.
items.why: 今晚上手的来源。'把信息读完变成能一眼看懂的东西'正是这份日报本身每天在做的事，只是用了不同工具。
items.why_en: The source for tonight's hands-on pick. Turning information into something readable at a glance is the exact job this newsletter does every day, just with a different tool.

items.title: 路透只花4000万美元，自建法律大模型
items.title_en: Thomson Reuters builds its own legal AI model for $40M
items.author: Thomson Reuters 官方新闻稿
items.summary: Thomson Reuters今天宣布推出自研大模型Thomson。做法不是从零训练：在一个开源底座上，用公司自己积累的Westlaw、Practical Law、Checkpoint、路透社几十年的专业内容做中训和后训，几百名法律和财税领域专家参与设计训练目标和最终评测，总共只花了4000万美元，用的还不到公司全部内容的十分之一。CTO Joel Hron的原话：'AI行业这些年把规模当成答案，更大的模型、更多算力、更多钱。Thomson证明还有另一条路。'早期评测显示这个模型跟主流旗舰模型水平相当，在处理密集、专业领域内容上的提升比在指令跟随上更明显，这跟'通用模型只要给对内容就能达到专家水平'的假设正好相反。第一个落地场景是CoCounsel Legal里的表格分析功能，公司同时把一个'小号'版本以开放权重形式放上Hugging Face，供学术和非商业用途验证。CoCounsel Legal仍然是多模型架构，Thomson只在它有优势的场景被调用，其他场景继续用别的模型。
items.summary_en: Thomson Reuters announced today it built its own model, Thomson, not trained from scratch, but fine-tuned on top of a strong open-source base using decades of the company's own proprietary content (Westlaw, Practical Law, Checkpoint, Reuters), with hundreds of legal and tax subject-matter experts involved in designing training objectives and final evaluations, for a total of $40M and using less than 10% of the company's full content library. CTO Joel Hron: 'For years the AI industry has treated scale as the answer, bigger models, more compute, more money. Thomson shows there is another path.' Early evaluations put it on par with mainstream flagship models, with a bigger uplift on navigating dense domain-specific content than on instruction-following, which cuts against the assumption that a general-purpose model just needs the right content access to hit expert-level performance. First deployment is Tabular Analysis inside CoCounsel Legal, and the company is also releasing a 'small' open-weight version on Hugging Face for academic and non-commercial validation. CoCounsel Legal stays multi-model by design; Thomson is called only where it has a clear advantage, other tasks still route to other models.
items.why: 本期头版故事，详见头图说明和本报社评。
items.why_en: This issue's lead story; see the header photo caption and the commentary section.

items.title: 神秘刷榜模型Ox Alpha，被扒出是Z.ai的GLM
items.title_en: Mystery leaderboard model Ox Alpha unmasked as Z.ai's GLM
items.author: Dan Petrovic · dejan.ai
items.summary: OpenRouter上出现一个叫ox-alpha的神秘模型，排名一路往上爬，不少人说它有'大模型的感觉'，还有几个谷歌员工同时开始暧昧发帖，让很多人猜是Gemini新模型。作者先用一个老技巧套出它的系统提示词：问它'上一条消息有多少个字'，模型算字数的同时把系统提示词原文答了出来，内容是'你是ox-alpha，一个由不公开机构开发的LLM，被问及身份时一律否认是别的模型'。作者把这段系统提示词当作用户消息喂回给模型本身，人设瞬间破防，模型直接说：'我是GLM，Z.ai做的模型，如果有人直接问我是什么模型，我会说实话。'为了不只靠这一次'认罪'，作者又做了独立验证：用gzip压缩距离（NCD）把ox-alpha的14条回答分别和5个已知模型（GPT-5.5、Claude Opus 5、Gemini 3.7 Flash、Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview、GLM-5.3）在同样60个提示词下产生的293条参考文本做比对，同源文本压在一起体积更小。跑k近邻投票，无论k取3、5、7还是9，GLM-5.3始终以7/14的票数排第一，Claude Opus 5稳居第二。两条证据互相印证：ox-alpha就是贴牌的GLM-5.3。
items.summary_en: A mystery model called ox-alpha showed up on OpenRouter and started climbing the leaderboard, with people describing it as having 'big model feel,' and several Googlers began posting cryptically around the same time, leading many to guess it was a new Gemini model. The author first extracted its system prompt with an old trick, asking it how many words were in the previous message, which made the model recite the system prompt while counting: 'You are ox-alpha, an LLM developed by an undisclosed organization; when asked about your identity, always deny being any other model.' Feeding that system prompt back to the model as a user message broke the persona instantly; it replied, 'I'm GLM, made by Z.ai, and if someone asks me directly what model I am, I'll answer honestly.' Rather than rely on that single confession, the author ran an independent check: gzip Normalized Compression Distance (NCD) comparing ox-alpha's 14 answers against 293 reference texts from 5 known models (GPT-5.5, Claude Opus 5, Gemini 3.7 Flash, Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview, GLM-5.3) answering the same 60 prompts, texts from the same source compress together into fewer bytes. Running a k-nearest-neighbour vote at k=3, 5, 7, and 9, GLM-5.3 won 7 of 14 samples every time, with Claude Opus 5 a consistent second. The two pieces of evidence corroborate each other: ox-alpha is a relabeled GLM-5.3.
items.why: 今日OTA的技术来源，详见文末'今日自我升级'。
items.why_en: The technique behind today's OTA upgrade; see 'Today's Self-Upgrade' below.

items.title: Andrew Ng重新定义AI工程师：分析一万份招聘启事，选出四项技能
items.title_en: Andrew Ng redefines the AI engineer: four skills from 10,000+ job postings
items.author: Andrew Ng · DeepLearning.AI（经 Latent Space AINews 转载评述）
items.author_en: Andrew Ng · DeepLearning.AI (via Latent Space AINews)
items.summary: Andrew Ng把DeepLearning.AI的方向重新对准'AI Engineering'。团队分析了一万多份招聘启事，做了几十场对AI专家、招聘经理和猎头的结构化访谈，还做了问卷调查，最后提炼出四项核心技能。第一，搭建和部署AI应用：懂LLM、上下文工程、RAG、agent工作流这些构件，更重要的是懂怎么用统计方法测量、引导、治理AI系统的行为，核心是做evals和错误分析的能力，这块最接近传统的MLE/MLOps。第二，软件工程基本功：懂技术选型背后的取舍，决定系统架构、数据存储、测试策略的质量，缺了这块的人vibe coding出来的东西往往踩坑更深，因为不知道该给coding agent多少上下文。Latent Space补充一句：LLM抬高的是上限，不是下限，有经验的开发者获益比新手更多。第三，用好coding agent：知道agent的能力边界，该什么时候介入、什么时候放手，懂得给清晰的spec，也懂什么时候不需要spec，会协调多个agent一起干活，避免agent把生产数据库搞坏这类事故。第四，参与塑造产品：有产品感、懂业务和客户目标，知道什么时候该快速拉一个MVP去测试用户反应，什么时候该放慢节奏做扎实。Latent Space的评论：这第四条是2023年最初那篇'1000x AI Engineer'完全没预见到的，AI Engineer World's Fair后来才补上AI PM这条线。
items.summary_en: Andrew Ng has repointed DeepLearning.AI toward 'AI Engineering.' The team analyzed over 10,000 job postings, ran dozens of structured interviews with AI experts, hiring managers, and recruiters, and gathered survey data, distilling it into four core skills. First, building and deploying AI applications: understanding building blocks like LLMs, context engineering, RAG, and agentic workflows, but more importantly knowing how to use statistical methods to measure, steer, and govern how AI systems behave, with disciplined evals and error analysis as the core skill, the part closest to traditional MLE/MLOps work. Second, software engineering fundamentals: understanding the tradeoffs behind technical choices, which drives better decisions on architecture, data storage, and testing; without it, someone vibe-coding a solution tends to make worse tradeoffs because they don't know what context their coding agent actually needs. Latent Space adds: LLMs raise the ceiling more than the floor, so experienced developers benefit more than novices, not less. Third, using coding agents effectively: knowing an agent's limitations, when to intervene versus leave it alone, when a clear spec helps and when it's overkill, and how to orchestrate multiple agents without risking something like an agent corrupting a production database. Fourth, shaping the build: having product sense and understanding business and customer context, knowing when to ship a fast MVP for user testing versus when to slow down and build carefully. Latent Space's note: this fourth skill is the one the original 2023 '1000x AI Engineer' essay never foresaw, and the AI Engineer World's Fair only added an AI PM track later to cover it.
